## Proof

We take the standard Hilbert product norms on the two product spaces:

$$\|(\phi_0,\phi_1)\|_1 = \bigl(\|\phi_0\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\phi_1\|_{H^{-1}}^2\bigr)^{1/2}, \qquad \|(f_0,f_1)\|_2 = \bigl(\|f_0\|_{L^2}^2 + \|f_1\|_{H^1_0}^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

**Step 1 — Bound each term of the duality product from above.**

By the dual-norm estimate for the $H^{-1}\!-\!H^1_0$ pairing,
$$\langle \phi_1, f_1\rangle_{H^1_0,H^{-1}} \;\le\; \bigl|\langle \phi_1, f_1\rangle_{H^1_0,H^{-1}}\bigr| \;\le\; \|\phi_1\|_{H^{-1}}\,\|f_1\|_{H^1_0}.$$

By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in $L^2(\Omega)$,
$$-\int_\Omega \phi_0\, f_0\, dx \;\le\; \Bigl|\int_\Omega \phi_0\, f_0\, dx\Bigr| \;\le\; \|\phi_0\|_{L^2}\,\|f_0\|_{L^2}.$$

**Step 2 — Combine and apply Cauchy–Schwarz on $\mathbb{R}^2$.**

Adding the two estimates,
$$\bigl\langle (\phi_0,\phi_1),(f_0,f_1)\bigr\rangle \;\le\; \|\phi_1\|_{H^{-1}}\,\|f_1\|_{H^1_0} \;+\; \|\phi_0\|_{L^2}\,\|f_0\|_{L^2}.$$

Set
$$a = \bigl(\|\phi_0\|_{L^2},\;\|\phi_1\|_{H^{-1}}\bigr) \in \mathbb{R}^2, \qquad b = \bigl(\|f_0\|_{L^2},\;\|f_1\|_{H^1_0}\bigr) \in \mathbb{R}^2.$$

The right-hand side above is exactly the Euclidean dot product $a\cdot b$. By Cauchy–Schwarz on $\mathbb{R}^2$,
$$a\cdot b \;\le\; |a|\,|b| \;=\; \bigl(\|\phi_0\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\phi_1\|_{H^{-1}}^2\bigr)^{1/2}\bigl(\|f_0\|_{L^2}^2 + \|f_1\|_{H^1_0}^2\bigr)^{1/2} \;=\; \|(\phi_0,\phi_1)\|_1\,\|(f_0,f_1)\|_2.$$

**Conclusion.** Chaining the inequalities,

$$\bigl\langle (\phi_0,\phi_1),(f_0,f_1)\bigr\rangle \;\le\; \|(\phi_0,\phi_1)\|_1\,\|(f_0,f_1)\|_2$$

for all $(\phi_0,\phi_1)\in L^2(\Omega)\times H^{-1}(\Omega)$ and $(f_0,f_1)\in L^2(\Omega)\times H^1_0(\Omega)$. The inequality **holds**. $\blacksquare$
